stories.title: Virginia Becomes Latest State to Enact 'Clean Slate' Law, to Help Residents Move on from Minor Offenses
stories.label: government
stories.summary: Virginia just put a new law into effect that automatically seals thousands of old misdemeanor convictions from public view. That means people who made a small mistake years ago no longer have it show up when they apply for a job, an apartment, or a loan. The sealing happens automatically, so nobody has to hire a lawyer or navigate paperwork to get this second chance. It's part of a growing wave of states giving people a real path forward instead of a permanent record holding them back.
stories.why_good: A real law took effect that directly removes a barrier to jobs and housing for thousands of people, with no downside and no political fight attached.
